key_insight: Combining hand-pointing cues with spoken references in egocentric video enables more precise and unambiguous object grounding than text-only methods.
problem_solved: Addresses linguistic ambiguity and the omission of non-verbal deictic cues in traditional visual grounding by introducing a multimodal framework that leverages hand-pointing plus speech in first-person (egocentric) settings.
method: EgoPoint-Ground: collect and release the first large-scale egocentric dataset with synchronized video, hand-pointing signals, and speech-based referring expressions.
Annotate and align modalities (hand keypoints/deictic gestures, speech transcripts, and object bounding boxes) to create grounding supervision for ambiguous references.
Provide multimodal baselines and evaluation protocols that fuse visual, linguistic, and deictic (hand) cues to benchmark egocentric referring expression grounding.
impact: Enables more robust, real-world referring systems for AR, assistive devices, and human-robot interaction by reducing ambiguity and leveraging natural deictic behaviors; provides a benchmark to drive multimodal grounding research.
visual_elements: Egocentric frame annotated with hand skeleton, pointing vector, speech transcript, and target bounding box (step-by-step overlay).
Dataset summary infographic: number of clips, annotated gestures, speakers, and average referring length (bar/stack chart).
Model/benchmark schematic showing fusion of vision, speech, and hand-pointing streams into a grounding prediction module.
Qualitative examples: success vs failure cases comparing text-only grounding vs hand+speech grounding.
paper_title: Beyond Language: Grounding Referring Expressions with Hand Pointing in Egocentric Vision
paper_authors: Ling Li, Bowen Liu, Zinuo Zhan, Peng Jie, Jianhui Zhong
